explain.met: The parcel is inside the city boundary, so Salt Lake City rules apply.

rules.title: Residential zone allows a basement apartment

explain.met: State law makes one internal accessory unit a permitted use in residential zones.
explain.not_met: This zone is not primarily residential, so state law does not make the unit a permitted use.
explain.unknown: We could not read the zone for this parcel. Ask the city to confirm it is residential.

explain.met: These units go inside a primary single-family home.
explain.not_met: Duplexes, townhomes and other buildings are outside what we have reviewed.
explain.unknown: Tell us the kind of home so we know which rules apply.

rules.title: Owner lives on the property

explain.met: You will live in the main house, so the owner-occupancy rule is met.
explain.not_met: Salt Lake City generally limits renting this kind of unit to owner-occupied homes. Ask the city whether an exception fits you.
explain.unknown: Salt Lake City generally requires the owner to live on the property, with some exceptions. Tell us if you will.

rules.nextAction: Ask the city which owner-occupancy exceptions apply and how to document that you live there.

explain.met: Cities may ban rentals shorter than 30 days. Your plan is long-term.
explain.not_met: Rentals under 30 days can be banned. Plan on 30 days or more.
explain.unknown: Tell us how long each rental would be.

rules.title: One extra parking space

explain.met: You have room for the extra on-site space a city may require.
explain.not_met: A city may require one more on-site space. Ask whether an exception applies.
explain.unknown: The city may require one more on-site space. You weren't sure, so the city should confirm.

rules.nextAction: Ask the city whether the unit needs one extra on-site parking space at this address.

rules.title: Building, fire and egress codes

explain.unknown: An inspector checks the emergency-exit window, ceiling height and smoke alarms. A photo can help you prepare.
